collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS — HUMOR AND ABSURDITY (HUM-01 to HUM-50, draft for the owner, 2026-11-15)
Slapstick, silly noises, puns, pranks with permission, ridiculous coincidences, a little funny magic and animals being absurd. Nobody is the butt of the joke: everyone keeps their dignity, and the comedy needs no victim.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. Edit anything and send it back; nothing ships until you approve.

ledger.why: the casting line, carried out as the roles' ages (picks two villagers aged 10 or older)

collection.description: A villager tries the new rope swing and the rope is far too long: hold on, or let go.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: Someone has tied a new rope swing to a branch over the lagoon. (subject) takes a run, grabs the rope and swings out over the water in a great arc. The rope turns out to be a good deal longer than anyone measured. First (subject)'s feet hit the water, then (subject.his/her) knees, and then (subject.he/she) is being towed slowly through the lagoon, still holding on, like a very surprised fishing lure.

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: (subject) holds on. The swing carries (subject.him/her) back, dripping, to the bank, where (subject.he/she) lets go and stands up with as much dignity as (subject.he/she) can find. (friend) shortens the rope. The next swing is perfect. Everyone still likes the first one better.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: (subject) lets go and sinks gently into the warm, shallow water, then bobs up, spits out a mouthful of lagoon, and announces, "It works!" The children line up at once, every one of them insisting on the long rope. Nobody shortens it all season.
